history: Luoyang is a cradle of Chinese civilization — the River Chart and Luo Book appeared here. Thirteen dynasties made it their capital over 1,500 years: the earliest and most of any city. The Lushena Buddha of Longmen has smiled for a millennium; White Horse Temple was China's first official Buddhist temple. Tang Luoyang was a center of the world — 'ask not of rise and fall; just look at Luoyang.'
importance: Capital of thirteen dynasties · Millennium imperial capital · City of peonies
foods: A 24-course state-banquet water banquet with soups between dishes.
Radish carved as peony — the water banquet's headliner.
Luoyang's morning soup culture — sweet or salty, add noodle strips freely.
Mung-bean pancakes in sour-spicy soup — a night-market legend.
Xiaojie potstickers — crispy base, juicy filling, garlic dip.
Pepper soup thickened with meatballs — the Luoyang way.
Pastry stuffed with peony petals — the flower aroma floats.
scenes: World Heritage — the Lushena Buddha's thousand-year smile.
China's first ancient temple — where Buddhism arrived.
Relics of thirteen dynasties, with fine Tang tri-color wares.
Where Guan Yu's head is buried — a shrine of Guan Yu culture.
'Skip Lijing Gate and you skipped Luoyang' — old town and night market.
Taoist holy mountain — golden roofs above a sea of clouds.
Famous central-plains mountain with waterfalls and cloud seas.
Restored Sui-Tang city gate with a stunning light show.
